title: Honoring Gold Star Mothers and Families
intro: Observed annually on the last Sunday in September, Gold Star Mother's and Family's Day honors the mothers and families of service members who gave their lives in service to our nation.

sections.heading: Remembering Those Who Served
sections.markdown:
Every fallen service member leaves behind a story, a legacy, and a family forever changed by loss. The courage of Gold Star families is reflected in the way they continue to honor their loved one's life and service while carrying their memory forward.

For the Marine Corps, remembrance is more than an annual observance. It is a continuing responsibility to honor the service of our fallen Marines, preserve their legacy, and remain connected to the families who stood beside them throughout their military journey.

sections.heading: Standing with Gold Star Families
sections.markdown:
Gold Star mothers and families will always hold a special place within the Marine Corps community. Their sacrifice is part of our shared history, and their connection to the Corps does not end with the loss of their Marine.

Across the nation, military organizations, local communities, and survivor support programs observe Gold Star Mother's and Family's Day through ceremonies, remembrance events, and personal outreach. These acts serve as meaningful reminders that the lives, service, and sacrifice of the fallen continue to matter.

On this day, we honor the Marines we have lost, recognize the families who carry their memory, and reaffirm that their service and sacrifice will always be remembered.

The [Marine Corps Long Term Assistance Program (LTAP)](https://www.usmc-mccs.org/ltap) supports surviving Marine Corps families by sharing information about Gold Star events across the country and connecting families with resources, support, and opportunities to remember their loved ones.

If you are a surviving Marine Corps family member interested in attending a local Gold Star event or learning more about available resources, contact LTAP at 866-210-3421 (Option 2).
